Khatir, Z., Thompson, H., Kapur, N., Toropov, V. and Paton, J. (2013). Multi-objective Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) design optimisation in commercial bread-baking. Applied Thermal Engineering 60(1-2), 480-486 (available online 23 August 2012). doi:10.1016/j.applthermaleng.2012.08.011

Background, no technology-level data. CFD and surrogate-model (moving least squares, genetic algorithm) optimisation of nozzle diameter, nozzle-to-band distance and jet velocity for temperature uniformity in a generic impingement oven. It prints no oven energy per tonne, cost, capacity or efficiency; the only energy figures are an estimated 10% saving for the baking process (a measure, already printed again in the held journal successor of Khatir 2012a, khatir_2013_001) and a reprinted whole-bakery range. What it has: Abstract and conclusions: about 10% energy savings achievable for the baking process (temperature-uniformity optimisation); 5-10% reduction in baking time for a surface-to-chamber difference of 10-20 degC (p.485). Bread production energy 5-10 MJ/kg, half used in the oven (p.480, reprinted from Thumann & Mehta 2008). Optimised designs: D = 20 mm, H/D = 7.75, u = 31.68 m/s (constrained); uniformity functional 1.16-1.31 (Table 2). Locators are printed journal pages 480-486. Id note: UKERC short form Khatir et al. 2012b; the journal volume year is 2013 (id kept as khatir_2012_003, file stem uses 2012, the online date).
